analysis: Examined both workflow metadata, the complete dev caller BASE/HEAD, and all supplied reusable-workflow patch hunks. The old secret-free branch build/master publication separation (BASE release-dev-branch.yml:78–83,234–239) is replaced by dev-push execution, a same-commit reusable workflow, write permission and secret inheritance (HEAD:47–58,95–106). This changes release-key, signed-artifact and qualification trust assumptions (A-005/A-011/A-017, T-054); a Developer ID signature still does not itself grant App Attest serving permission (T-052/T-056). release-provider.yml:142–145 passes the environment to verify-source; :829–834 adds an Apple/team/bundle designated requirement, strengthening final artifact verification but not protecting secrets from edited workflow logic. No supplied change directly alters hop encryption, runtime plaintext handling, billing or local hold/fan controls. Integration must inspect the full reusable workflow, master verify-source implementation and resolver changes to confirm source/qualification binding, lane isolation, artifact provenance and publication serialization. Confirm actual dev rules and secret/environment restrictions: comments are evidence of intent, not verified live configuration. Those material contracts remain unresolved in this bounded source pass.

findings.detail: A push to dev invokes the reusable workflow from that same commit (line 103) with all inheritable repository secrets (line 106) and contents:write. Previously, arbitrary branch code built without release secrets, while credentialed publication ran master's scripts. A compromised account able to update dev can now modify release-provider.yml in the pushed commit to export inherited credentials or misuse the shared Apple signing identity; it can also remove the purported master-script source gate before execution. Setting environment:dev does not constrain which inherited secrets a modified callee can reference. The new comments explicitly describe repository-wide secrets and a dev branch without enforced review, although live rules need confirmation. Keep credentialed workflow logic at a trusted, reviewed revision, pass only necessary lane-specific secrets, and enforce reviewed branch/environment approval before granting access to shared signing credentials. Update the release trust contract to describe this expanded authority.
findings.title: Dev-controlled reusable workflow now inherits repository release secrets
